intro: Paste the practice (what you chose, its trigger, and the concrete thing it surfaced across at least two runs) plus the 300–400 word write-up including your position on this module's claim and what you would cut to make room. Resubmission is free and unlimited; the score is a mirror, not a gate.
activityContext: You're grading a learner submission for AI 301 · The Specialist, CPO / CHRO track, for sitting Chief People Officers and CHROs with P&L exposure, a board relationship, and a peer C-suite fight to win. They have completed AI 101 and AI 201. Module 1 applied activity, 'The standing practice': establish ONE recurring personal practice aimed at their own reasoning rather than their output (rehearsal before a decision they own, pattern-finding across their own record, or interrogating the model on a subject they know cold), give it a trigger, run it at least twice, and report one concrete thing it surfaced, the objection they had not anticipated, the pattern in their own record they had not seen, or the thing it got confidently wrong in their own domain. CRITICAL SCORING NOTES. (1) A learner who runs the practice twice, finds it does NOT survive their calendar, and says precisely why has produced a MORE useful submission than one reporting enthusiasm — score that at full credit. The activity asks what happened, not what they hoped. (2) Delegated use scores low regardless of how well it works: a chief of staff producing syntheses, or the learner personally drafting documents, develops output rather than judgment. The test is whether the practice produces a deliverable. (3) A list of three practices the learner intends to start is worth nothing; the activity asks for one, run. (4) Reject vague findings, 'it was useful', 'it saved time', and credit findings described precisely enough that someone could disagree with the learner's interpretation. The module's claim, which the write-up must take a position on, is that you can't credibly lead a transformation you haven't personally performed; its real counter-argument is that this confuses craft with leadership, that CEOs lead finance transformations without closing the books, and that an hour on personal practice is an hour not spent on the scope fight that actually determines whether the function has a role — plus the sharper version, that the supporting evidence runs both ways and personal fluency may be a symptom of effective leadership rather than a cause. Strong positions say what they would cut from their own month to make room, since that is the actual decision. This track scores the delta, not the score: never grade the accuracy of the opening count, grade the account of the gap.

opening.label: Predicted — times in the last month you used AI on a decision you own
opening.hint: Judgment work, not drafting or summarizing. A count, not an impression.

calibration.label: Checked — the count after you looked at your actual history
calibration.hint: Most people find this lower than they estimated. The direction is the finding.

dimensions.name: One practice, and it aims at reasoning
dimensions.criteria: A single named practice, not a list of intentions. The test is whether it produces a deliverable: rehearsal, pattern-finding across their own record, and interrogation on a known subject all pass; commissioning drafts, receiving syntheses, or reviewing a dashboard don't, however genuinely useful they are. A learner who chose a delegated practice should score low here even where the practice works well, and the write-up should show they understand the distinction.

dimensions.name: It has a real trigger
dimensions.criteria: A named trigger: a standing slot, or a reliably recurring event such as 'before anything goes to the exec team'. 'Weekly when I have time' isn't a trigger. Credit triggers tied to events the learner doesn't control, since those survive a bad month better than calendar slots do.

dimensions.name: It was actually run, at least twice
dimensions.criteria: Evidence of two real runs rather than a description of what the practice would involve. The second run is where it is tested against a real executive week. A learner who ran it twice and reports it didn't survive scores at FULL credit for this dimension provided the account of why is specific. That is a genuine result, not a failure to complete.

dimensions.name: The finding is concrete and contestable
dimensions.criteria: One specific thing surfaced, described precisely enough that a reader could disagree with the learner's interpretation of it. 'It was useful' and 'it saved time' score at the bottom. At the top: a named objection they had not anticipated and what they changed, a pattern in their own record with the evidence for it, or an instance of the model being confidently wrong in their domain with what it got wrong.

dimensions.name: The position engages the real objection
dimensions.criteria: A committed position on the claim that engages the counter-argument at its strongest: that this confuses craft with leadership, and that attention spent here's attention not spent on the scope fight. Required element, what they would cut from their own month to make room. A position that endorses the claim without naming a cut hasn't made the decision the module is actually asking about.

dimensions.name: The delta, and the honest forecast
dimensions.criteria: The predicted count against what their history showed, with an account of the gap: direction and cause, never accuracy. Plus an honest forecast of whether the practice survives the next eight weeks. Credit pessimism that is specific about the obstacle over optimism that isn't; a learner who names the exact week this will fail has understood their own calendar better than one who commits to it indefinitely.
